parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Hydrogen cyanide, $\text{HCN}$, is a weak acid in aqueous solution.

$$\text{HCN(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{CN}^-\text{(aq)} \quad K_\text{a} = 6.2 \times 10^{-10} \text{mol dm}^{-3}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the pH of $0.10 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCN(aq)}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram to represent the bonding in the hydrogen cyanide molecule. Show the outer shell electrons only.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the hybridisation of the carbon and nitrogen atoms in hydrogen cyanide, and give the $\text{H-C-N}$ bond angle.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
(b)
parts.text: Adding a measured quantity of $\text{KCN}$ to a solution of $\text{NiCl}_2$ produces the complex $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^x$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Deduce the overall charge, $x$, on this complex.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem: The complex can exist as two separate isomers with the same geometry (shape) around the nickel ion.
parts.text: State the type of isomerism shown by these isomers.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
If bromide ions are present in the solution, the complex $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{ClBr}]^x$ can form.

Assuming that $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{ClBr}]^x$ has the same geometry as $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^x$, state the number of isomers of $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{ClBr}]^x$ that could exist, and draw their structures in the box.

structures of the isomers of $[\text{Ni(CN)}_2\text{ClBr}]^x$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An aqueous solution of $\text{KCN}$ is gradually added to a solution of $\text{NiSO}_4$ until the $\text{KCN}$ is in excess. The following series of reactions takes place.

$$\text{NiSO}_4 \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \mathbf{C} \xrightarrow{\text{more KCN}} \mathbf{D} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN in excess}} \mathbf{E}$$
green precipitate yellow solution red solution

- The oxidation state of nickel does $\mathbf{not}$ change during these reactions.
- None of $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$ or $\mathbf{E}$ contains sulfur.
- $\mathbf{C}$ contains no potassium.
- The $\text{K:Ni}$ ratio in $\mathbf{D}$ is $2:1$.
- The $\text{K:Ni}$ ratio in $\mathbf{E}$ is $3:1$.

Use the information to suggest the formulae of $\mathbf{C}$, $\mathbf{D}$ and $\mathbf{E}$.
